root_cause.producer: EpisodeManager.tick broadcast one TICK_SYNC per server tick at 20 Hz with no back-pressure
root_cause.consumer: MineOccludeClient.onFrame polled exactly one PendingTick per client tick
root_cause.why_permanent: Production and consumption rates were equal, so the queue had no drain margin. Any backlog accumulated during client startup or a render stall persisted for the whole episode instead of catching up.
root_cause.consequence: The framebuffer read always returned the CURRENT world while the state row it was joined to was the OLDEST queued tick. The image therefore depicted a strictly later world than its own state row, and every visibility, coordinate, and target decision read it as if it showed that row.
not_the_cause: PNG encoding is already off the render thread and cannot change what was photographed
the index join was structurally consistent: server_epoch_nanos identical across streams for 260/260 rows, render_frame_idx equal to row index, streams strictly monotonic

repair.server_behaviour: After broadcasting TICK_SYNC for tick N the recorded episode arms a gate and performs no sheep step, no state row, no camera re-assert and no tick increment until the acknowledgement for N arrives. An acknowledgement for any tick other than the outstanding one is ignored, so a duplicate or straggler cannot release the gate early.
repair.client_behaviour: Acknowledges immediately after the framebuffer read completes and before off-thread PNG encoding, so the stall lasts only as long as the capture itself.
repair.fail_closed: A client that stops acknowledging fails the episode after 400 server ticks rather than recording unaligned frames.
repair.per_frame_evidence_added: tick_queue_depth_at_capture, enforced by validate_capture_temporal_alignment; under lockstep it is always 0 and any nonzero value is a refusal

cadence_impact.reason: Every recorded tick still advances the target by speed * 0.05 blocks. The lockstep gate changes only how long a tick takes in wall-clock, never how far the world moves per tick.

secondary_defect_repaired.evidence: client mods carried an Aug 10 build while the server carried an Aug 14 build
secondary_defect_repaired.consequence: the two sides ran different builds and no client-side capture change could reach the process that takes the screenshots
secondary_defect_repaired.repair: ProductionCaptureWorker._ensure_started now installs the governed JAR into both runtime roots and verifies both by hash

changed_governed_files.change: new client to server acknowledgement packet
lockstep gate, ack handler, fail-closed timeout
send acknowledgement after framebuffer read; log queue depth
